source_text: Si enim secundum carnem vixeritis, inquit, moriemini: si autem spiritu facta carnis mortificaveritis, vivetis ideo dici carnem concupiscere, quia carnaliter anima concupiscit?
pass_a_gloss: If for according-to flesh vixeritis, he-says, moriemini: if however spiritu made of-flesh mortificaveritis, vivetis for-that-reason dici flesh concupiscere, because carnaliter soul concupiscit?

lemmas.lexica: LS anima; Blaise human soul as image

pass_b_english: The flesh is said to desire because the soul desires in a fleshly way.
The baptized person has nothing left to put to death.

choices.why: Image of God in the soul; keep soul not 'mind' or 'life-force'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
